questions.note: Order and cascade follow the scan: the hallux just ahead of toe 2 and touching it, toes 3-5 stepping back, toe 5 rolled outward. Individual shaping is weak. Toes 2-4 are near-identical straight columns with no knuckle hump. The lateral tips are crimped in V3, the plantar pads look like stacked pills, toe 5 has a ring at its base, and the lesser toes are slimmer than the scan's.

Heel, malleoli and Achilles follow the scan closely. From behind, the medial bulge sits higher and in lower relief; the lateral sits lower, more prominent and further back (V2/V3). The Achilles is a broad cord with hollows on both sides, and the column now sits over the heel. No anterior ankle crease shows in clay at the front of the ankle in V2, V3 or V1f.

defects.what: Toes 2-4 are three near-identical, straight, parallel columns with level tops and no PIP knuckle hump; the scan's toes each swell at the knuckle and flare into a round pulp, and no two are alike.
defects.fix: Give each lesser toe its own dorsal PIP hump behind the nail fold, a slight downward curl to the tip and its own width and taper, following the scan's bulbs.

defects.what: In the lateral view the lesser toe tips are thin and crimped, with sharp top edges, lower and flatter than the scan's round, full bulbs at the same place.
defects.fix: Keep the scan's toe volume there: round full pulps with soft outlines, the tips as thick as the scan's.

defects.what: Toe 5 meets the forefoot through a crisp vertical ring near its base, like a tube plugged into a sleeve; the scan's toe 5 runs into the forefoot with no edge.
defects.fix: Blend the toe's base into the forefoot over several millimetres, with no ring or step.

defects.what: From below, toes 2-5 are stacked pills with crisp transverse ring creases and hard outlines; the scan's plantar toes are each one plump pad behind a soft sulcus.
defects.fix: One full plantar pad per toe, a soft sulcus at the base, and at most faint flexion creases.

defects.what: Small, sharp, hook-shaped notches sit at the roots of the webs between toes 2-3, 3-4 and 4-5, also visible in V1f.
defects.fix: The web roots are soft, shallow U-shaped saddles of skin.

defects.what: A short, sharp mark across the hallux's plantar pad reads as a cut, not a soft flexion crease.
defects.fix: A shallow, soft-edged IP crease, or none at this scale.

defects.what: Fine contour-like ripple rings on the back of the hallux (and around its tip in hr.plan) are a displacement artefact, not skin wrinkles.
defects.fix: Smooth skin, or a few irregular transverse wrinkles over the IP joint only.

defects.what: From above, crisp crinkle lines and dark slits at the bases of toes 3, 4 and 5 make the lesser toes read as separate fingers; the scan's toes merge into the forefoot through soft webs.
defects.fix: Soft webs that close between the toes' bases, as the scan's do.

defects.what: A small speck of background still shows between the hallux and toe 2 in the plantar silhouette: a pinhole where the two should touch.
defects.fix: Close the contact so the silhouette is solid between hallux and toe 2.

defects.what: The lateral toes that peek past the heel are crinkled with sharp ridges, crisper than the scan's soft rings at the same place.
defects.fix: The same round, soft toe bulbs as the scan's.

defects.what: In the proportion view the lesser toes are slimmer and more separate than the scan's fat, pressed-together bulbs, with a crisp notch at each web root, so the forefoot reads more delicate than the scan's.
defects.fix: Keep the scan's toe girth and the toes pressed together; only the nails and fine relief should be new.

ranked: [D11] In V1f, the view for proportion, the lesser toes are slimmer, more separate and more delicate than the scan's thick, pressed-together toes. The forefoot reads younger and finer than a boot-wearing man's.
[D1] Toes 2-4 are near-identical straight columns with no knuckle humps. Real toes (scan and photographs) each bulge at the PIP joint, curl slightly and differ in width and taper.
[D2] In the lateral view the lesser toe tips are thin, flat and crimped with hard edges, where the scan has round, full pulps.
[D4] From below the toes are stacked pills with crisp ring creases; real plantar toes are one plump pad each behind a soft sulcus.
The toes are crisp and hard-edged while the rest of the foot is soft scan surface. They read as a separate sculpt grafted onto the scan, not one continuous skin.
[D3] Toe 5 has a crisp ring at its base in V3, like a tube in a sleeve; the scan's runs into the forefoot without an edge.
[D8] From above, crisp crinkles and dark slits at the bases of toes 3-5 make the lesser toes read as fingers rather than toes pressed together.
[D5] Sharp hook notches at the web roots (V5f, V1f) where real webs are soft saddles.
[D7] Contour-ripple rings on the back and tip of the hallux read as a displacement artefact.
[D6] A sharp slit-like mark across the hallux's plantar pad reads as a cut.
[D10] The lateral toes seen past the heel in V8 are crinkled and sharper than the scan's at the same place.
[D9] A pinhole of background between hallux and toe 2 in the V4o silhouette, where they should touch.

No anterior ankle crease shows at the front of the ankle in V2 or V3. The hard transverse line across the mid-instep in V1f (the venous arch, out of scope) reads as a fold and breaks the dome of the dorsum.
Context: from below (V4, V4o) spec 03's calf stands well past the foot's medial border near the heel and hides the medial heel and arch outline, so the plantar silhouette cannot be compared there.
